title: Linked Lists (Singly, Doubly, and Circular)

singly_linked_list.name: Singly Linked List
singly_linked_list.definition: A Singly Linked List is a linear dynamic data structure composed of nodes where each node contains data and a single pointer (`next`) pointing to the succeeding node in sequence, ending with NULL.
operations: Insertion at End: O(n) without tail pointer, O(1) with tail.
Insertion at Position: O(n) traversal to (pos - 1).
Deletion from End: O(n) traversal to second-last node.
Reversing List: O(n) time using 3 pointers (prev, curr, next).
singly_linked_list.sample_io:
Output:
Initial list: [5] -> [10] -> [20] -> [30] -> NULL
After deleting head: [10] -> [20] -> [30] -> NULL
Reversed list: [30] -> [20] -> [10] -> NULL
singly_linked_list.dry_run:
Reversing list [5 -> 10 -> 20 -> 30]:
Initial: prev=NULL, curr=5
Pass 1: next=10, 5->next=NULL, prev=5, curr=10
Pass 2: next=20, 10->next=5, prev=10, curr=20
Pass 3: next=30, 20->next=10, prev=20, curr=30
Pass 4: next=NULL, 30->next=20, prev=30, curr=NULL
Loop terminates. Return prev (30). List is reversed.
singly_linked_list.time_complexity:
• Insert at head: O(1)
• Insert at tail: O(n)
• Search: O(n)
• Reverse: O(n)
singly_linked_list.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space (O(n) total memory for nodes)

viva_questions.q: How many pointers are required to reverse a singly linked list iteratively?
viva_questions.a: Three pointers: `prev` (tracks preceding node), `curr` (tracks current node), and `next` (preserves remaining list before breaking the link).

viva_questions.q: What is the difference between an array and a linked list?
viva_questions.a: Arrays have contiguous memory, fixed capacity, and O(1) random access. Linked lists have scattered heap memory, dynamic capacity, O(n) sequential access, and O(1) insertions once the target node is found.

doubly_linked_list.name: Doubly Linked List (DLL)
doubly_linked_list.definition: A Doubly Linked List is a linear data structure where each node contains three fields: a data value, a pointer to the previous node (`prev`), and a pointer to the next node (`next`), enabling bidirectional traversal.
doubly_linked_list.advantages: Bidirectional traversal (forward and backward), O(1) deletion of a given node pointer without needing the preceding node pointer.
doubly_linked_list.disadvantages: Higher memory overhead (2 pointers per node instead of 1), extra pointer operations on insertions/deletions.

viva_questions.q: What is the primary advantage of a Doubly Linked List over a Singly Linked List?
viva_questions.a: A node in a Doubly Linked List can be deleted in O(1) time if given its direct pointer, because `node->prev->next = node->next`. In a Singly Linked List, you must traverse from the head in O(n) to find the predecessor.

circular_linked_list.name: Circular Linked List (CLL)
circular_linked_list.definition: A Circular Linked List is a linked list variant where the last node points back to the first node (head), forming a continuous circular loop with no NULL termination.
circular_linked_list.applications: Round-robin CPU process scheduling, multiplayer board games (turn rotation), media playlist looping.

viva_questions.q: How is a Circular Linked List traversed without an infinite loop?
viva_questions.a: Record the pointer to the head node. Use a `do ... while (curr != head)` loop so that iteration stops when the pointer loops back to the start.
